item.title: Overcoming ATH anxiety: Why automated DCA is the safest way to buy Bitcoin near all-time highs
item.content:encoded:
Back in November 2021, when Bitcoin was hovering just under $69,000, I was absolutely terrified to buy, convinced the market would crash the moment I did. That paralyzing fear of buying at the peak is incredibly common. But once I realized the math behind overcoming ATH anxiety: why automated DCA is the safest way to buy Bitcoin near all-time highs, I stopped stressing and let my system do the work.

I ended up waiting for weeks back then, watching the price tick up, and then finally FOMO'd in at the absolute worst moment anyway. It was a classic rookie mistake. I tried to time the market, failed, and felt sick to my stomach when the price started sliding downwards.

If I had just set up a recurring buy, my average entry price would have been significantly lower. Here is why the math works, and how you can get past the mental barrier of buying when prices are breaking records.

The math of buying the absolute top

Let's look at what actually happens if you start buying at the peak. Most people think that if you buy at an all-time high, you are doomed to hold bags for years. But if you are using dollar-cost averaging (DCA), the math works out completely differently.

If you put a lump sum in at the peak, yes, you are down. But if you split that money into weekly buys, you buy fewer fractions of a coin at the top, and significantly more as the price drops. Your average cost basis falls rapidly.

You can actually model this yourself using a cycle-aware Bitcoin DCA calculator to see how quickly your portfolio recovers even if your start date was the worst possible day of the cycle. In fact, during previous cycles, investors who started a weekly DCA at the absolute peak were already back in the green long before Bitcoin reached its previous peak again.

Overcoming ATH anxiety: Why automated DCA is the safest way to buy Bitcoin near all-time highs

So here's the thing: mainstream crypto advice always tells you to "buy the dip." I think this is actually terrible advice for most regular people. Why? Because when the dip actually happens, fear takes over. You start thinking, "What if it goes lower?" and you don't buy. Then, when the price starts pumping to new highs, you get anxious again and think, "I missed it, I'll wait for the next dip."

You end up stuck in a loop of doing absolutely nothing.

This is why overcoming ATH anxiety: why automated DCA is the safest way to buy Bitcoin near all-time highs became my personal mantra. By automating the process, you remove the decision-making entirely. You aren't choosing to buy at $70k or $90k; your system is just executing a plan.

I prefer to buy on a reliable platform with deep liquidity. If you don't have an account yet, you can set up an account on Binance to get started. But the key is to make sure those buys happen automatically, without you having to log in and look at the chart.

Taking my own emotions out of the equation

To be honest, I got so tired of fighting my own psychology that I decided to build my own solution. I wanted something that would connect to my exchange API, execute my buys quietly in the background, and automatically send the coins to my cold storage.

That's why I built a free tool to automate my Bitcoin purchases. It connects to your exchange, lets you set your schedule, tracks your progress toward personal life goals, and gets on with its day.

Of course, buying is only half the battle. You also need to keep those coins safe. I never leave my coins on exchanges for long. I always withdraw them to a secure Trezor hardware wallet for peace of mind.

Obviously, I'm not your financial advisor—do your own research and only invest what you can afford to lose. But for me, letting go of the need to time the market was the best decision I ever made. It turns out that consistency beats cleverness every single time.

If you want to take the manual work out of DCA, I built a free tool that automates the whole process — connects to your exchange, buys on schedule, withdraws to your wallet.
